title: The bandaged volunteer miracle cure routine
summary: Doc Moon hired a down-and-out man, wrapped him in bandages and staged a miracle cure to sell tonic.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But this medicine show, let me finish telling you...
Yes, that's what I wanted, to get the end of that.

Another one of the things that really got 'em... Doc would go into St. Louis or one of them places, and find some bum hanging around the poor part of town, or Skid Row as you call it, and tell him he had a job for him if he wanted to make three or four dollars and get a good meal. And he also had a portable wheelchair in this bus, you see. So when he got in there, the deal was to strip down to his underwear, and Doc had bandages. He'd wrap this cat all up in these bandages, from head to foot. Then he'd have somebody wheel him: "Make way, we've got a real sick fellow here." And we had some big boards that we'd roll him up on the bandstand. And this guy had a routine down perfect. Most of them would be shaking, like, [GESTURES] "Lord have mercy." Doc says, "How you feel there, fella? This man is sick. How do you feel there, sir." "Oh, Doc, I'm in bad shape. I'm in bad shape. Can you help me, Doc, please?" -- he's pleading. Doc says, "Well, I think I can help you. Moon's Tonic has never failed me yet. Moon's Tonic!" -- shake it up. The guy says, "Please, Doc. Please. Please give me a little of it." And so Doc says,
"All right." Doc says, "Now, if Moon's Tonic can help this poor fellow, you see his misery, he's dying, he's literally dying..."
Think what it can do for you.

You got it. Doc pulled out a great big spoon and gave him a shot of it. And Doc says, "How do you feel?" "Oh, I feel better, a little better, Doc. Can I have another one of them." And Doc gives it to him, and he says, "Lord have mercy, Doc, give me the bottle, I feel so good." Half of the time, Doc wouldn't have nothin' but whiskey in there, because that was all he started with. [LAUGHING] And this guy would take that stuff and drink it, and people...[LAUGHS HARDER]...was just hypnotized lookin' at him! "Looka that. Isn't that somethin'? That's a miracle." Then the guy says, "How you feel?" How do I feel, Doc? I feel like dancin'!" And he'd start peeling these bandages off, you see. Doc says, "Oh yeah? Why don't you show these people how good you feel. Now, this fella, he's cured. Look at him." "I want to do a buck-and-wing there, Doc. Light up something, hit me a tune." And we'd play "Twelfth Street Rag," and this guy would jump all around, and then Doc would say, "That's enough. Get the hell off the stand. Get off this stand. You did it."
He'd suffer for humanity to put up with things like that. Oh, good God almighty.
[LAUGHING] That's the God's truth. When they first told me they did that, I said, "No, you guys can't pull that crap." They said, "You'll see."
It stretches your imagination, but there's no better to put over someone than a big one...
And he sold a ton of medicine! But like I said, a lot of people...you'd have to pay the sheriff off, you see. They knew it was just a con game.
